Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field with 2 years of experience; or Master’s Degree with no additional experience.

Proficiency in Python and backends like FastAPI.
Proficiency in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript; experience with React, or similar.
Experience building applications that consume ML/AI models via REST APIs or SDKs
Familiarity with ML concepts and tools (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, MLflow) and generative AI/LLM application patterns.

Strong data visualization and UX design sensibility.
Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with technical and non-technical partners

title: Associate Director, Enterprise Forecasting Platform Product Owner
location: Mettawa, IL, US
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose:
AbbVie’s Global Forecasting Center of Excellence (COE) sustains and advances the organization’s volume forecasting capabilities established under Finance Transformation Forecasting Excellence. The COE defines forecasting standards, governs best practices, oversees deployment of enabling technologies, executes centralized forecasting functions on behalf of the organization, and builds forecasting competencies across AbbVie’s US, International, and Allergan Aesthetics commercial organizations.
The COE’s Operations & Insights pillar is the operational and analytical engine that powers enterprise forecasting at scale, encompassing AI and statistical modeling and governance, forecasting platform management, and centralized analytics. The Enterprise Forecasting Platform team is a key component of the COE and is responsible for the business ownership, operation, adoption, and continued evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform.
Position Overview
The Associate Director, Enterprise Forecasting Platform Product Owner is accountable for the business ownership, strategy, ongoing management, and evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform. The role owns the product vision and roadmap, prioritizes capabilities and enhancements, drives adoption and effective utilization, oversees platform economics, and ensures the product continues to meet evolving enterprise forecasting needs.
This role serves as a key business owner of the relationship with the platform vendor. It establishes platform performance expectations, manages service levels and commitments, oversees adoption and utilization measures, and ensures AbbVie realizes appropriate value from its investment.
The Product Owner works closely with forecasters, Finance leadership, Forecasting COE teams, Business Technology Solutions (BTS), data and analytics partners, Procurement, and the platform vendor to translate business needs into platform priorities and deliver an effective foundation for enterprise forecasting processes.
Core Job Responsibilities:
Enterprise Product Ownership & Strategy
Serve as the business product owner for AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform, accountable for overall business value, usability, adoption, and continued evolution.
Define and maintain the product vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Global Forecasting COE priorities and enterprise business needs.
Develop and manage strategic and tactical roadmaps that translate forecasting needs into sequenced platform capabilities and enhancements.
Own business prioritization of platform features, functionality, integrations, and enhancements.
Maintain and prioritize the business product backlog in partnership with BTS, the vendor, the COE, Finance, and forecasting stakeholders.
Establish clear prioritization criteria based on enterprise value, user impact, cost, risk, implementation complexity, and operational readiness.
Evaluate opportunities to expand or improve platform capabilities as forecasting processes, analytical methods, data availability, and technologies evolve.
Vendor & Commercial Management
Own the strategic business relationship with the enterprise forecasting platform vendor and serve as the primary point of accountability for vendor performance.
Define, monitor, and enforce vendor success measures and service-level agreements (SLAs).
Establish regular vendor governance and performance reporting covering enhancements, defects, service levels, contractual commitments, open issues, risks, and remediation plans.
Hold the vendor accountable for delivery against agreed priorities, timelines, service expectations, and contractual obligations.
Partner with Procurement, BTS, Finance, Legal, and other functions on contract renewals, commercial discussions, and vendor evaluations.
Monitor platform consumption and contractual usage where applicable and identify potential cost, capacity, or service implications.
Maintain visibility into total product cost and value, including vendor fees and associated investments required to operate and enhance the platform.
Assess whether the vendor roadmap and capabilities remain aligned with AbbVie’s evolving forecasting needs.
Platform Implementation, Operations & Continuous Improvement
Oversee the business implementation of platform releases, enhancements, and new capabilities, ensuring solutions meet agreed requirements and compliance expectations.
Partner with BTS and the vendor to translate forecasting needs into clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation priorities.
Establish processes for intake, triage, prioritization, escalation, and resolution of platform issues and enhancement requests.
Monitor platform performance and user experience, identifying recurring friction points and opportunities to simplify or improve forecasting workflows.
Ensure platform changes consider impacts to upstream data, forecasting processes, analytical outputs, downstream planning activities, and end users.
Maintain product documentation, decision history, requirements, roadmap materials, operational procedures, and key institutional knowledge.
Drive continuous product improvement.
Adoption & Capability Building
Partner with COE and the Forecast Excellence team to champion the forecasting platform across the organization, create a clear understanding of its value and appropriate use, and identify and address barriers to adoption.
Develop a structured approach for measuring platform adoption, utilization, user experience, and business value.
Build feedback mechanisms that allow forecasters and Finance stakeholders to influence product priorities while maintaining disciplined enterprise governance.
Translate platform capabilities into clear, practical implications for forecasting teams.
Stakeholder Management & Governance
Act as the primary business interface among forecasting users, COE leadership, Finance leadership, BTS, data and analytics teams, Procurement, and the platform vendor.
Capture and synthesize requirements from brands, geographies, and forecasting teams into enterprise-level priorities.
Proactively manage expectations regarding roadmap priorities, delivery timing, platform limitations, dependencies, and tradeoffs.
Establish transparent governance for major product decisions and investment priorities.
Regularly communicate the product roadmap, progress, risks, adoption, issues, vendor performance, and business value to COE and Finance leadership.
Co-Lead workshops and decision forums (in partnership with Standards and Training) needed to align stakeholders around product choices and future capabilities.
Escalate material platform or vendor risks and drive them through resolution.
Financial & Resource Management
Develop and manage the business case and budget associated with the enterprise forecasting platform.
Maintain transparency into platform costs, vendor spend, enhancement investments, and required resources.
Evaluate the costs, expected benefits, and organizational implications of significant platform enhancements and investments.
Partner with Finance, BTS, Procurement, and COE leadership to inform investment and resource-allocation decisions.
Identify opportunities to improve the economic efficiency of the platform while protecting critical enterprise forecasting capabilities.
Team / People Leadership
Lead and guide team members supporting forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support as the operating model evolves.
Own prioritization and work planning for the team, ensuring resources are allocated to the highest-value platform needs.
Provide regular feedback, coaching, and career-development support to team members.
Build strong product-management capability within the Operations & Insights organization.
Create a culture of user orientation, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Reporting
Reports to: Director, Forecasting Operations & Insights
Direct reports: Team members supporting enterprise forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support, with size determined by the evolving operating model.
ualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Analytics, Information Technology, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in product management, platform ownership, forecasting, analytics, technology-enabled business transformation, or related roles.
Demonstrated experience owning or managing a complex enterprise technology product or platform through implementation, adoption, optimization, and ongoing evolution.
Demonstrated ability to develop product strategies and roadmaps and translate business needs into prioritized technology capabilities and requirements.
Experience managing external technology or platform vendors, including performance, delivery commitments, issue escalation, and commercial considerations.
Strong understanding of enterprise data, analytics, technology, and the dependencies required to operationalize technology-enabled business processes.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with business, data, analytics, and technology teams and translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to lead complex, matrixed initiatives involving multiple stakeholder groups and competing priorities.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder-management skills, including experience communicating product decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders.
Ability to operate effectively under ambiguity, make disciplined prioritization decisions, and manage multiple concurrent priorities.
Preferred:
Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, life sciences, or another complex global commercial organization.
Experience with commercial forecasting, financial planning, analytics, or decision-support platforms.
Familiarity with pharmaceutical volume forecasting and planning cycles such as LBE, Plan, and LRP.
Experience managing enterprise software-as-a-service platforms and vendor relationships.
Experience establishing product governance, adoption metrics, service expectations, and product-performance reporting.
Experience working with forecasting or planning technologies and their supporting data ecosystems.
Familiarity with AI, machine learning, and statistical forecasting capabilities and how they integrate into enterprise forecasting workflows.
Experience managing platform budgets, contracts, business cases, and technology investment decisions.

The Market Research and Analytics Manager will support launch readiness and commercialization for a key oncology asset by delivering actionable analytics, performance reporting, and data-driven insights. This role will develop and maintain launch and KPI dashboards, help automate recurring reporting over time, and partner across APEX and cross-functional teams to strengthen analytics and AI capabilities.
The Manager will serve as a hands-on analytics partner with a strong pharmaceutical analytics background, ideally in oncology or hematology. This individual will understand the multiple myeloma market, translate business questions into practical analytical solutions, and communicate findings clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. The role will work closely with management, Centers of Excellence, Digital Lab, Omnichannel Analytics, data partners, and Franchise M stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
Launch analytics and KPI reporting. Develop and maintain launch and KPI dashboards for a key oncology asset that provide timely visibility into business performance and key launch indicators. Partner with stakeholders to define business requirements, metrics, data sources, and reporting needs.
Reporting automation and scalability. Support the long-term automation and evolution of launch reporting tools to improve efficiency, reliability, scalability, and usability. Help establish repeatable processes, quality checks, documentation, and appropriate governance for recurring reporting.
Business analytics and decision support. Build a strong understanding of the multiple myeloma market, the oncology asset strategy, and commercial priorities. Translate business questions into structured analytical approaches, synthesize findings across sources, and generate actionable insights and recommendations.
Analytics and AI capability advancement. Partner with Analytics Centers of Excellence and other internal experts to identify business-relevant opportunities, evaluate new analytical approaches, and support responsible adoption of approved AI tools and capabilities within the team.
Digital and omnichannel analytics. Serve as the primary day-to-day Insights and Analytics point of contact for Digital Lab and Omnichannel Analytics partners supporting non-personal promotion (NPP) analytics, with management guidance and support. Translate business needs into clear analytical requirements and connect findings to broader the oncology asset strategy and execution.
Pharmaceutical data expertise. Apply working knowledge of patient-level claims and other pharmaceutical data sources, including DDD, specialty pharmacy (SP), specialty distributor (SD), and Xponent, to address business questions. Understand the appropriate uses, strengths, and limitations of available data and engage subject-matter experts when needed.
Cross-functional partnership. Build effective working relationships across Franchise M, APEX, Finance, Digital Lab, Centers of Excellence, technology and data teams, and external analytics partners to ensure analytics are coordinated, relevant, and aligned with business priorities.
Communication and storytelling. Translate complex analyses into clear, concise business implications and recommendations. Develop high-quality written deliverables and presentations and communicate effectively with both analytical and nontechnical audiences.
Bachelor's degree in analytics, data science, statistics, economics, business, life sciences, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Demonstrated experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology analytics, ideally within oncology or hematology, with a strong understanding of commercial business questions and market dynamics.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical solutions and actionable recommendations.
Experience developing dashboards, KPI reporting, performance measurement, and automating recurring business reporting using Claude Code or similar GenAI tools
Strong business acumen and ability to understand market dynamics, customer needs, brand strategy, and commercial priorities.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, and data-storytelling skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings to nontechnical stakeholders.
Strong collaboration, project management, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and with technical partners.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain attention to analytical quality, and deliver against timelines with appropriate independence.
Experience supporting product launches, launch dashboards, KPI frameworks, or omnichannel and non-personal promotion (NPP) analytics.
Experience evaluating or adopting approved AI-assisted analytics, coding, or productivity tools in partnership with technical experts or Centers of Excellence.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with patient claims and pharmaceutical commercial data sources, including DDD, specialty pharmacy (SP), specialty distributor (SD), Xponent, promotional activity, healthcare professional, account, or sales data.
Experience specifically supporting oncology product launches, launch analytics, or hematology markets.
Working knowledge of SQL, Snowflake, Python, or comparable analytical tools and data platforms is a plus, but not required.
Experience with reporting automation, self-service analytics, or data quality and validation processes.

Launch and KPI dashboards for a key oncology asset are delivered on time, meet stakeholder needs, and provide reliable visibility into launch performance.
Recurring reporting becomes more efficient and scalable through appropriate automation, documentation, and quality controls.

Partnerships with Centers of Excellence, Digital Lab, Omnichannel Analytics, and cross-functional stakeholders result in well-coordinated analytical support.
New analytics and approved AI capabilities are adopted responsibly where they create meaningful business value.

As defined in the scope of the assigned development project(s), the Medical Director, Clinical Development will have global responsibilities and fulfill the following roles:
Therapeutic Area Medical Director (TAMD)
With supervision, the Medical Director oversees the planning, execution and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of a clinical development program. The TAMD participates in cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and interpret high-quality clinical data supporting overall product medical, scientific and business strategy, all while providing mentorship and guidance to junior team members where needed.
The TAMD may be asked to participate in internal process improvement activities within R&D and the wider organization, as well as external interactions with KOLs and Regulatory authorities.
The employee must conduct their work activities in compliance with all relevant laws, regulations, and regulatory guidelines as well as all AbbVie policies and procedures.
Note: While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add or remove duties from a particular job and to assign other duties as necessary and at any time.

As Sr Principal Engineer Black Utilities, you will be a global technical authority for AbbVie’s non-product contact process utilities, including plant steam, condensate, waste water, vacuum, compressed air and process chillers. You will lead Black Utilities workstreams on complex brownfield and greenfield projects, from feasibility and basis of design through construction, commissioning, qualification and handover, while developing standard designs, verifying calculations, leading design reviews, resolving troubleshooting and root cause issues, and mentoring engineers. Partnering with Strategic Investments, sites, Quality, EHS, Validation/CQV, MS&T and external firms, you will advise leadership and influence cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority. If you are an experienced utilities engineer who enjoys solving complex problems at global scale in a regulated environment, this role offers broad influence on projects that ultimately serve patients.
Global Engineering Context
Global Engineering provides engineering leadership, technical governance, standards development and project execution support across AbbVie’s global manufacturing network and strategic investment portfolio.
The organization supports greenfield manufacturing facilities, new technology platform deployments, brownfield expansions, modernization programs, debottlenecking initiatives, lifecycle asset replacement, infrastructure upgrades and capacity expansion investments.
Global Engineering roles are expected to promote common standards, transfer lessons learned across regions and sites, and enable consistent engineering delivery across strategic capital investments.
Key Responsibilities
Global Technical Execution Support
Lead Black Utilities workstreams for complex brownfield and greenfield capital projects from feasibility and front-end planning through BOD design stage of the project. Provide technical support during detailed design, construction, commissioning, qualification, startup, and handover.
Develop, maintain and deploy standard designs and philosophies associated with non-product contact process utilities generation and distribution including plant steam, condensate, waste water collection and neutralization, vacuum, compressed air, process hot water/ glycol and process chillers
Partner with Key stakeholders including operators, system owners, quality, and third party design firms.
Provide risk based technical input for system commissioning and qualification in support of URS’s, Risk Assessments, Functional Requirements, Verification protocols, PQ’s.
Provide technical leadership for utility operation and maintenance troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and remediation.
Independently verify design calculations and assumptions including hydraulic calculations, diversifications, and system modeling.
Lead multidisciplinary design reviews, constructability reviews, code evaluations, vendor technical evaluations, and technical bid analyses. Resolve advanced non-compliant or constrained existing conditions using risk-based engineering judgment.
Ensure engineering deliverables comply with AbbVie standards, approved project requirements, EHS requirements, and relevant codes and industry practices. Document assumptions, rationale, calculations, risks, decisions, and recommended mitigations.
Advise leadership on complex technical decisions, alternatives, risks, cost and schedule impacts, reliability implications, sustainability opportunities, and operational readiness. Escalate issues with clear evidence and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate scope, interfaces, deliverables, technical resources, schedules, and discipline budgets with project managers, site engineering, operations, Quality, Validation/CQV, EHS, MS&T, architects, other engineering disciplines, EPCM firms, vendors, and OEMs.

AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.

Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.

Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.

Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.

title: RF Hardware Engineer - Multi-Radio Coexistence
location: Cupertino
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? As a member of our dynamic group, you will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of Apple’s customers every day!
Our RF Systems Engineering team is looking for a passionate, self-motivated individual to work on overall system performance of multi-radio coexistence for various wireless technologies (e.g., Cellular, Wi-Fi, BT, GPS, NFC).
You will be responsible for assessing platform-level multi-radio coexistence performance, including:
- Performing HW failure analysis at the RF/wireless system level to understand low margin or failing behaviors making use of hands-on experimental modifications to hardware.
- Proposing design and process changes for multi-radio coexistence issues considering design constraints and align with cross-functional partners on trade-offs and implementation path.
- Reviewing designs and sign-off on releases of PCB layouts, flex layouts, system level groundings, shielding.
- Execution of validation & characterization test plans to meet multi-radio coexistence performance targets.
- Tracking validation status, analyze results and communicate insight from data.
- Evaluating multi-functional change requests and update characterization plans as needed, highlight any issues.
- Working with RF Test Engineers to bring-up device-under-test, setups and test procedures for multi-radio coexistence validation.
- Performing simple experiments using hardware mock-ups, system prototypes and experimental setups.
- Collaborating with cross-functional partners for circuit-level, system-level simulations to understand risk areas and root cause issues.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering with 10+ years relevant work experience.
Experience on at least one radio of Cellular, GPS, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Thread, NFC, and UWB.
Knowledge of RF component characteristics and experience using lab equipment including spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, signal generator and oscilloscopes.
Knowledge of wireless architectures including front-end, antenna sharing, link budget line-up.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 20%.
Preferred qualifications: Master’s degree in electrical engineering with 10+ years relevant work experience.
Experience working with chipset teams to define RF/wireless system-level requirements and influence chipset architecture or design decisions.
Proven understanding of RF hardware and standard methodologies for system-level grounding, shielding, isolation, and electromagnetic interference mitigation.
Experience performing hands-on disassembly and system level debug on module, reference board or system level.
Experience debugging and performing optimizations at the conducted or radiated radio systems level.
Excellent communication written and verbal skills.

title: Project Leader - Principal Investors Private Equity and Financial Institutions
location: Summit, New Jersey, United States of America
description: Who We Are Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact. To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures - and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive. Practice Area BCG is supporting the world's largest principal investors & private equity (PI) firms with the full spectrum of services covering the entire value chain from transaction services to transformative profit improvement programs for portfolio companies to strategy and operations work for the funds themselves. We are organized into six distinct sectors: Private Equity, Sovereign Wealth Funds (SWFs), Pension Funds, Hedge Funds, Family Offices and Infrastructure & Real Estate. What You'll Do As a member of our consulting team, you will manage the design and development of long-term business strategies for private equity and financial institutions client in the areas of go-to-market strategy, operating model design, organizational design, and value creation in order to optimize revenue growth and organizational capability. Specific duties include: perform sophisticated market research, benchmarking, market sizing, modeling, forecasting, and decision analysis to identify growth opportunities; lead buy-side and sell-side commercial due diligence for private equity clients across the deal lifecycle, including building bottom-up and top-down market sizing models, mapping competitive landscapes and market share dynamics, and assessing target companies' growth drivers, customer concentration, and pricing power to inform investment committee recommendations and valuation assumptions; manage procurement transformation workstreams across multiple spend categories for financial institution clients, including diagnosing current-state procurement structure and category management maturity, defining future-state specifications and sourcing strategy, and running vendor consolidation efforts from market scan through RFP design, bid evaluation, and negotiation; serve as PMO lead for financial institution transformation programs spanning multiple workstreams and spend categories, coordinating communication and reporting cadence with senior client leadership, tracking cross-category dependencies and milestones, and preparing steering committee materials to keep executive stakeholders aligned on decisions and progress; manage case team responsibilities including personnel assignments, research and analysis, and reports to clients; undertake critical evaluation of analytical work performed using advanced economics and financial analysis techniques; oversee and direct consultants and junior professional staff, and oversee project planning and preparation of outputs; and present findings to senior client management, and oversee business development and client relationships. What You'll Bring The position requires a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Management, or related field (willing to accept foreign education equivalent) plus three (3) years of experience as a management consultant or business analyst which must include at least one (1) year of experience providing business strategy recommendations focusing on operational efficiency and revenue growth to companies in the private equity and financial institution sector. Specific skills/other requirements (quantitative experience requirement not applicable to this section) - must possess the following: analyzing Nielsen consumption data, including purchase trends, market share, and category dynamics, to build bottom-up and top-down market sizing models and competitive benchmarks for buy-side and sell-side private equity due diligence; conducting detailed market research, including interviewing technical experts on specialized and complex topics, to synthesize findings on demand forecasts, market expansion opportunities, competitive positioning, M&A decisions, and synergies between companies for the investment thesis; leveraging Python to build and execute end-to-end RFP processes for procurement vendor consolidation, including generating RFP documentation, aggregating and cleaning supplier response data, and analyzing bid results against cost and qualitative criteria; building Excel-based cost and spend models using client procurement data across multiple spend categories to compare current-state vendor terms against future-state sourcing scenarios, quantify savings opportunity, and identify vendor consolidation and category management strategy; conducting branch and ATM network optimization analysis, including evaluating customer demand patterns, transaction volumes, and terminal proximity/overlap across the network, to develop consolidation recommendations that balance cost savings with customer access; coordinating PMO reporting and communication across multiple workstreams and spend categories for senior client leadership, including milestone tracking and steering committee material preparation; applying advanced economic and financial analysis theories including competitive cost and decision analysis, capabilities assessment, portfolio review based on financial reports, and experience and scale curve analysis; conducting advanced analysis of scale economies, seasonal effects on financial forecasts, impact of uncertainties on business outcomes, corporate financing policies, and evaluation of factors that influence a company's debt capacity; and managing individuals, teams and processes. Additional info Multiple positions available. Applicants will only be considered for Summit, NJ office location. Partial telecommute benefit available. Must report to and reside within commutable distance of the listed BCG office. Domestic/international travel required (up to 80%) based on client/company need. M-F, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. 45+ hours per week. Salary range: $225,400.00 - $252,900.00 per year. In addition to your base salary, you will also be eligible for an annual discretionary performance bonus and BCG's Profit Sharing and Retirement Fund (PSRF) contribution. BCG also provides a market leading benefits package described below. We pay the full cost of medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees - and their eligible family members. * That's zero dollars in premiums taken from employee paychecks. Low $10 (USD) copays for trips to the doctor, urgent care visits and prescriptions for generic drugs. Dental coverage, including up to $5,000 (USD) in orthodontia benefits. Vision insurance with coverage for both glasses and contact lenses annually. Reimbursement for gym memberships and other fitness activities. Job Summary
Cox Automotive is hiring a Portfolio Manager to support the assigned Colorado Springs, Colorado Territory .  The Portfolio Manager is responsible for managing and growing our $100k to $2.5M within the assigned geographic territory.  The primary responsibilities include building and maintaining relationships with clients, optimizing the portfolio through the clients’ use of the line of credit, identifying and mitigating pre-default account risk and supporting post default collections on defaulted accounts.
Candidates must live within the zip codes related to the Territory.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Optimize each client’s use of the line of credit within an assigned portfolio whose lines of credit range from $50k to $2.5M by acting as a floor plan subject matter expert to their portfolio of clients.
Achieve goals and performance targets as set by the company by regularly engaging with clients in person or virtually and by collaborating with internal partners to drive revenue and maximize profitability through prudent account management, controlled growth and risk mitigation.
Educate clients on desired performance behaviors, self-service options, and best practices and coach them to ensure compliance with company policies and expectations.
Collect and analyze client financial information and various internal reports and dashboards to assess add monitor dealer performance and address with the dealer as appropriate to drive growth and manage risk.
Support the Risk and Recovery department with pre-default risk mitigation and post default collection efforts on defaulted accounts.
Serve as a fiduciary for the company including identifying and reporting to the company any material client or internal non-compliance with company policies, attempted or actual fraud upon the company or any other circumstance that may require identification and reporting to protect the company.
Support the Risk and Recovery department with pre-default risk mitigation and post default collection efforts on defaulted accounts.
Document in Salesforce all activities and client interactions as required by the company.
Cox Automotive cross business unit relationships and opportunities.
Job Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Automotive industry (various sectors).
Finance industry (various sectors).
Strong financial acumen with working knowledge of key financial tools and terminology.
Strong presentation, verbal and written communication skills.
Strong interpersonal skills with ability to interact with clients, collaborate with internal team members. and external partners at various levels within the organization.
Strong time management skills with ability to manage deadlines.
Strong negotiation and collection skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently and in a remote environment.
Ability to maintain a high level of safety awareness and take necessary safety precautions.
Proficient in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and Salesforce.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in related discipline and 4 years’ experience in a related field (finance, client facing. B2B, account management and/or collections).
The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as a master’s degree and 2 years’ experience; a Ph.D. and up to 1 year of experience; or 8 years’ experience in a related field in lieu of a degree.
Automotive and/or floorplan industry background preferred.
Financial knowledge and acumen preferred.

description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:
At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-plus-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, advisory, and consulting groups as well as our enabling services functions. That’s why we continually invest in innovation, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.
Job Description:
About the Role
Crowe is seeking an experienced NetSuite Account Manager to help expand our NetSuite consulting practice through strategic alliance relationships, partner-driven business development, and consultative sales.
In this role, you will build and strengthen relationships with Oracle NetSuite account executives, territory and regional managers, and partner stakeholders to identify new client opportunities and position Crowe as a trusted implementation and advisory partner.
You will collaborate with Crowe's consulting leaders, solution architects, and delivery teams to develop joint go-to-market strategies, support complex sales pursuits, and grow our pipeline of NetSuite implementation and consulting opportunities.
The ideal candidate brings strong experience within the NetSuite partner ecosystem, excellent relationship-building skills, and a demonstrated ability to translate client business needs into consulting opportunities that drive long-term revenue growth.
What You'll Do
Build and maintain strategic relationships with Oracle NetSuite account executives, channel leaders, territory managers, and partner stakeholders to generate and advance new business opportunities.
Develop and execute joint go-to-market strategies with NetSuite and ecosystem partners to generate qualified pipeline and support co-selling initiatives.
Collaborate with NetSuite sales teams to identify prospective clients, understand business challenges, and position Crowe's NetSuite consulting and implementation services.
Lead early-stage client discovery conversations to understand financial and operational transformation needs and identify potential consulting opportunities.
Partner with Crowe solution consultants, presales architects, and delivery leaders to develop solution strategies, proposals, and sales presentations.
Manage and advance a pipeline of alliance-driven opportunities, supporting revenue targets and maintaining accurate account, contact, and opportunity information in the firm's CRM system.
Identify opportunities to expand relationships with existing NetSuite clients through additional implementation, optimization, advisory, and managed services offerings.
Represent Crowe within the NetSuite partner ecosystem through partner meetings, industry events, enablement programs, and relationship-building activities.
Collaborate with marketing and alliance leadership to support campaigns, partner events, and thought leadership initiatives that strengthen Crowe's market presence.
Maintain knowledge of NetSuite products, partner programs, ERP market trends, and competitive offerings to effectively position Crowe's services.
Required Qualifications
5+ years of professional experience in business development, alliance sales, partner management, enterprise software sales, or consulting services sales.
Demonstrated experience co-selling with Oracle NetSuite account executives or supporting joint go-to-market initiatives within the NetSuite partner ecosystem.
Proven ability to develop and maintain strategic relationships with alliance partners, client executives, and internal business stakeholders.
Experience supporting consultative sales cycles involving multiple decision-makers, technical stakeholders, and cross-functional teams.
Strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage effectively with client executives and partner stakeholders.
Experience collaborating with solution consultants, presales architects, and delivery teams to position consulting services and support complex sales opportunities.
Strong pipeline management and organizational skills, including experience using CRM systems to track opportunities, partner engagement, and sales activity.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and collaborate effectively in a fast-paced consulting environment.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed for partner engagement, client meetings, and industry events.
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
Experience working within the Oracle NetSuite, Oracle, or broader ERP/cloud software partner ecosystem.
Prior experience in consulting, professional services, or technology services sales.
Experience supporting ERP or cloud ERP transformation initiatives for mid-market organizations.
Familiarity with NetSuite solutions and competing ERP platforms, including Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Sage Intacct, Acumatica, or similar technologies.
Experience working with private equity-backed companies, high-growth organizations, or mid-market clients.
Familiarity with structured sales methodologies such as MEDDICC, Challenger, or comparable consultative sales frameworks.
Demonstrated success developing partner relationships, generating qualified sales opportunities, and supporting revenue growth.
Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, team-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities.
What Success Looks Like
Successful candidates will establish strong relationships within the Oracle NetSuite partner ecosystem, generate a consistent pipeline of qualified consulting opportunities, and help expand Crowe's NetSuite implementation and advisory services.
They will demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively with NetSuite sales teams and Crowe consulting professionals, advance partner-sourced opportunities, and strengthen Crowe's position as a trusted NetSuite implementation partner.
They will also contribute to sustainable revenue growth through effective pipeline management, joint go-to-market initiatives, client relationship development, and identification of additional consulting opportunities within existing accounts.
What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe: Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes. In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development. Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.
We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

Your exceptional people experience starts here. At Crowe, we know that great people are what makes a great firm. We care about our people and offer employees a comprehensive total rewards package. Learn more about what working at Crowe can mean for you!

title: Director; Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) (Remote)
location: Remote - USA
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
MISUMI Americas serves customers through regional sourcing teams and a network of QCTs (warehouses) that hold inventory close to demand. As the business grows, we need one clear, trusted process that connects what sales expects to sell with what we source, build and stock. This role creates and owns that process.
The Director, SIOP is the practice lead for Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning. Each month, they bring together a top-down view (business plan, targets, market signals) and a bottom-up view (account and regional forecasts) over a rolling horizon of six months or more. They turn that consensus demand into requirements by region and into the inventory each QCT must hold. Where supply cannot meet demand, they make the gap visible, size the impact on customer service and revenue, and consolidate the proposed fixes into clear investment options for the executive team.
The Director, SIOP is a peer of the Directors, Portfolio Management and works with them as partners. Portfolio Management owns what we offer: assortment, pricing, launches, exits and supplier capability. SIOP owns how much, where and when: consensus demand, regional supply requirements, QCT inventory targets and the monthly planning process. Phase 1 covers standard and configurable products and QCT inventory; custom process lines are covered through demand and partner-capacity visibility.
This is a Director role with a player-coach start: the person runs the process hands-on at first, then builds a small, highly capable team of planners and analysts. Success is measured by forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns.
Own the monthly SIOP cycle: Design, run and keep improving the monthly process end to end: data refresh, demand review, supply review, reconciliation and the executive SIOP meeting. Set the calendar, the inputs each team owes and the decisions each step must produce.
Own the consensus demand number: Combine the business plan and targets with account and regional forecasts from Sales and the category overlay from each Portfolio Manager (launches, price changes, exits, competitive moves). Reconcile the views, explain the gaps and agree one demand plan over a rolling horizon of six months or more. Sales owns the account forecast; Portfolio Managers own the assumptions in their overlay; SIOP owns the process and the final number.
Translate demand into regional requirements: Map the consensus forecast to supply requirements by region, so regional sourcing teams know what volume and mix they must secure, and when.
Set inventory policy and QCT targets: Define safety stock, reorder logic and stocking depth by QCT and SKU class, to meet the service levels agreed in the executive SIOP review within the working-capital envelope set by Finance. Portfolio Managers decide which items are in the stocked set; SIOP decides how deep and where. Plan the run-down of items Portfolio Management decides to exit.
Run the input scorecard: Track whether Sales, Portfolio Management and Sourcing deliver complete, on-time and credible inputs each month, and publish the scorecard. The VP, Portfolio Management is the executive sponsor, chairs the monthly review and escalates late or weak Portfolio Management inputs. Late or weak Sales inputs escalate to the executive leadership team through the scorecard. The SVP, Operations & Supply Chain co-sponsors the supply-side inputs (Sourcing and QCTs) and escalates those.
Find and size supply and demand mismatches: Identify where demand will exceed supply or capacity, or where we hold inventory that demand does not support. Quantify revenue at risk and service impact. The relevant Portfolio Manager proposes the fix for their category or process; SIOP consolidates the proposals into the executive pre-read.
Lead the executive SIOP review: Prepare a concise monthly pre-read and run the executive meeting. Frame the decisions needed (investment, allocation, stocking, capacity), record what was decided and follow up on actions to closure.
Own the planning metrics: Define, measure and report forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns. Set targets with the executive team and drive improvement over time.
Build the tools and data foundation: Work with Finance, Business Systems and Data teams to establish the planning data model, forecast history and dashboards the process needs. Choose and implement planning tools as the practice scales.
Build the team: Hire, develop and lead a small, high-performing team of demand and supply planners or analysts as the practice grows.
All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
Required
Experience: 10+ years in demand planning, supply planning, S&OP / IBP or supply chain operations, with at least 3–5 years leading the S&OP or SIOP process for a multi-region business.
Built a process before: A track record of designing and launching a monthly S&OP / SIOP cycle (not only taking part in one), and making it stick across sales, operations and finance.
Strong analytical skills: Fluent in forecasting methods, inventory policy (safety stock, service levels, reorder points) and capacity planning. Advanced Excel / Google Sheets; comfortable with BI tools and large data sets.
Influence without authority: Proven ability to hold sales and operations leaders accountable for inputs and commitments they do not report to you for.
Works as a peer of category owners: Gets the commercial story from category owners and stays out of assortment and pricing decisions.
Executive communication: Can turn complex planning data into a short, clear story with options and trade-offs for senior leaders.
Business judgment: Can build an investment case that links inventory and capacity decisions to service levels, revenue and working capital.
Leadership: Experience hiring and developing planners or analysts, or a strong readiness to build a team from scratch.
Education: Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, engineering, business or a related field.
Preferred
Industry: Experience in industrial distribution, manufacturing, configurable components or a high-SKU, make-to-order and stock business.
Network inventory: Experience setting inventory policy across a network of warehouses or distribution centers.
Planning tools: Hands-on experience with planning platforms (for example, Kinaxis, o9, Anaplan, SAP IBP or similar) and ERP data.
Global and matrixed work: Experience in a multinational company, including work with a parent company or stakeholders across cultures and time zones.
Certification: APICS / ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) or similar is a plus; an MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
AI and automation: Interest in using AI and automation to improve forecasting and reduce manual planning work.
Primarily remote, computer-based work, including extended periods at a computer and on video calls. Occasional visits to QCT (warehouse) and supplier sites, which involve walking, standing and following site safety rules.
Ability to travel up to 20% annually, mainly within the Americas, for QCT and regional sourcing visits, team meetings and offsites, with occasional international travel to work with MISUMI Group planning teams.
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs

We’re actively seeking teammates who:

ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Packaging Engineer to design, specify, and validate custom packaging for our Made-to-Spec (MTS) battery components. This role reports into our Supplier Industrialization Engineering team. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission! Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Translate requirements: work with Design Engineering to capture critical-to-quality (CTQ) needs for MTS parts (tolerances, surface finish, fragility) and turn them into clear packaging specifications.

 - Design custom packaging: create and revise dunnage, shipping racks, and containers in SolidWorks, with guidance from senior engineers, for domestic and international logistics.

 - Support suppliers: provide drawings, specs, and technical answers to packaging and component suppliers so they can source and build without ambiguity; follow up on open issues and sample builds.

 - Support industrialization: help run first-article and PPAP-style approvals for packaging assets and check that supplier processes meet capacity, quality, and durability needs.

 - Apply DFM/DFA: review designs for manufacturability and for how packaging interfaces with automated lines and line-side presentation at Form Factory.

 - Validate designs: plan and run ISTA/ASTM-based tests (drop, vibration, compression) with internal or third-party labs, analyze results, and drive design fixes.

 - Maintain documentation: keep packaging drawings, BOMs, specifications, and test records accurate and under revision control.

 - Improve continuously: track damage, density, and cost data, and propose practical improvements.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Packaging Engineering/Packaging Science preferred.

 - 4-7 years of experience in packaging, mechanical, or manufacturing engineering (automotive, supply chain, industrial, or similar high-volume manufacturing preferred).

 - Proficiency in ArtiosCAD, SolidWorks, CAPE (or similar CAD) and strong working knowledge of technical drawings and GD&T.

 - Working knowledge of packaging materials (aluminum, steel, composites, corrugate, foam, wood) and how they perform in transit; familiarity with ISTA/ASTM test methods.

 - Ability to manage multiple tasks, flag risks early, and communicate clearly with cross-functional teams and external suppliers.

 - Occasional travel to suppliers.

title: IT Systems & Automation Lead - Bolingbrook
location: Chicago, IL || Bolingbrook, IL
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI-native, technically resourceful operator to rethink how IT works at Formic. You'll own the day-to-day technology experience for Formicans, from devices, applications, and employee support to infrastructure, security fundamentals, and external technology partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with significant autonomy: you'll solve immediate problems while building smarter, more reliable systems that prevent them from recurring.
If the Wi-Fi is down, someone's account isn't working, a conference room isn't connecting, a new hire needs a laptop, or a critical application goes offline, you're the person who makes sure it gets handled. You aren't expected to personally pull every cable, configure every system, or solve every specialized security issue. You are expected to own the outcome.
You don't need to know every system we use on Day 1. We'd rather hire someone with strong technical fundamentals, exceptional resourcefulness, and an ability to learn quickly. Over time, we expect you to become an expert in Formic's technology environment and help shape how our systems evolve as we grow.
You do need to be highly capable at using AI to extend what you can do. We want someone who is genuinely excited about technology and constantly asks: Why are we doing this manually? Can I automate it? Can I make this better?
AI and automation are central to this job, not side projects. We want someone who connects AI to real systems and workflows, builds practical automations, experiments responsibly, and measures whether their work makes Formic faster and more effective.

Lead and support production team members to meet daily manufacturing targets.
Communicate shift goals, updates, and expectations clearly to team members.
Serve as a role model for attendance, performance, and workplace behavior.
Support shift handoffs by communicating key updates and issues to maintenance or supervisors.
Inspect boards and ensure visual and dimensional quality standards are met.
Use QA inspection tools to measure the quality of products.
Follow QA standards to ensure we are producing a quality product.
Provide proper training for all new end of line associates.
Monitor and provide coaching and feedback regarding work performance of end of line associates.
Communicate with extruder operators to ensure a quality end product.
Review work order and ensure correct tags and color.
Manage line documentation.
Ensure packaging specifications are met.

Adhere to Fiberon’s safety requirements.
Assist with managing the production floor (breaks, absences, etc.)
High school diploma or equivalent
Additional technical, manufacturing, or quality-related training preferred
EXPERIENCE
Minimum 1-3 years of manufacturing preferred
Previous experience in product inspection, stacking , packaging, or material handling preferred
Experience in composite decking, plastics, wood-plastic composites, or related manufacturing environments preferred
Prior leadership, training, or team lead experience preferred
WORK ENVIRONMENT
Manufacturing environment with exposure to: Heat, noise, dust, and moving machinery
May require availability outside of standard hours to support troubleshooting or continuous operations.

Strength & Endurance Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull objects weighing between 20 to 50 pounds independently (over 50 pounds with buddy lift), including cleaning equipment, dust collection systems, and raw materials.
Perform repetitive tasks such as sweeping, brushing, vacuuming, and operating tools like staple guns and banders.
Stand and walk for extended periods (8 to 12-hour shifts) during production and cleaning tasks.
Maintain stamina and focus to perform physically demanding tasks without fatigue.
Mobility & Flexibility Bend, squat, stoop, kneel, crawl, and stretch to reach and clean various areas, inspect equipment, and align materials.
Climb ladders and work at heights to access dust accumulation and perform maintenance tasks.
Reach or work above shoulder level as needed.
Dexterity & Coordination Use hand tools such as brushes, brooms, scrapers, and vacuums with precision and good hand-eye coordination.
Handle packaging materials, attach labels, and refill equipment accurately and efficiently.
Visual & Sensory Acuity Good vision required to identify dust accumulation, inspect product quality, and monitor screens and labels.
Ability to perform color and defect inspections with close attention to detail.
Maintain balance and spatial awareness to ensure safety and stability in a dynamic environment.
Environmental Tolerance Work in hot, noisy, dusty, and/or humid conditions for extended periods.
Tolerate exposure to moving mechanical parts, vibrations, and varying temperatures.
Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) such as masks, respirators, safety glasses, earplugs, and gloves for long durations.

Recognize personal physical limits and request assistance when tasks become too demanding.

Primary Function of Position
The Director, SEC Reporting & Technical Accounting is a highly visible leadership role with direct
responsibility for the credibility, clarity, and integrity of the Company’s external financial reporting.
Reporting to senior finance leadership, this individual leads SEC reporting and technical
accounting, advises executive management on complex and consequential matters, and serves
as a key partner to Investor Relations, Legal, cross-functional finance leaders, external auditors,
and outside counsel. The role offers a meaningful opportunity to shape how a global, innovative
company communicates its performance, accounting judgments, and evolving business model to
investors and other stakeholders. It is also a demanding role: success requires exceptional
technical judgment, disciplined execution, direct and thoughtful communication, and the ability to
remain composed and decisive through compressed filing timelines, significant transactions, and
changing regulatory expectations. The Director will build a high-performing team, strengthen
disclosure and internal-control processes, and create scalable, technology-enabled ways of
working without compromising quality.
Essential Job Duties
• Own the end-to-end preparation, review, and filing of Forms 10-K and 10-Q, earnings
releases, proxy-related financial disclosures, registration statements, and other current
reports. Set a high bar for technical accuracy, narrative clarity, consistency across public
communications, and on-time execution.
• Lead preparation and maintenance of support for the balance sheet, income statement,
statement of cash flows, statement of stockholders’ equity, earnings per share, and share-
based compensation disclosures.
• Translate complex business activity and accounting conclusions into clear, balanced, and
investor-relevant MD&A, financial statement footnotes, and other external and internal
reporting materials.
• Orchestrate a rigorous cross-functional review process with executive management,
Investor Relations, Finance, Legal, external auditors, and outside counsel. Surface issues
early, drive decisions, and resolve comments without sacrificing quality or control
discipline.
• Partner with Investor Relations on quarterly earnings scripts, supporting schedules,
investor presentations, and consistency checks across public communications.
• Oversee and review financial press releases and other public financial information
announcements.
• Lead the analysis and documentation of complex U.S. GAAP and SEC reporting matters.
Develop technically supportable, operationally workable conclusions and communicate
the implications to senior leaders in a direct and understandable way.
• Oversee accounting for share-based compensation, leases, strategic investments,
business combinations, goodwill, intangible assets, and other judgmental or non-routine
transactions.
• Lead implementation and monitoring of new accounting standards, including impact
assessments, implementation plans, policies, controls, disclosures, and cross-functional
communications.
• Own the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls within the function and
support Sarbanes-Oxley compliance.
• Build and sustain a high-performing team through thoughtful hiring, candid coaching,
meaningful development opportunities, clear priorities, and strong accountability. Create
depth and succession readiness across critical responsibilities.
• Redesign reporting and technical accounting workflows using automation, analytics, and
disciplined process improvement. Reduce low-value manual work while preserving
appropriate review, evidence, data integrity, and control ownership.
• Own the SEC reporting calendar, disclosure checklist, tie-out process, review protocols,
and evidence-retention standards, with clear milestones and accountability across
contributors.
• Oversee inline XBRL tagging and filing quality, including taxonomy selection, extensions,
validation, and coordination with the filing service provider.
• Support the Disclosure Committee and Audit Committee through concise summaries of
significant accounting judgments, new standards, filing developments, and key disclosure
matters, including cybersecurity disclosure support.
• Maintain and govern the technical accounting memorandum standards.
• Monitor SEC, FASB, PCAOB, and peer-company developments; assess emerging risks
and recommend timely changes to disclosures, policies, and controls.
• Partner with Business Development, Tax, Treasury, Legal, and business leaders on
transaction structuring and accounting for acquisitions, investments, and other
agreements.
• Establish reporting-process performance indicators, perform post-filing retrospectives, and
implement lessons learned.
• Represent the function with credibility during high-stakes reviews and discussions,
including matters involving executive leadership, the Disclosure Committee, external
auditors, and outside counsel.

• 14 or more years of progressive public accounting experience or a mix of public
accounting and public-company industry experience, including significant SEC reporting
and technical accounting leadership experience.

presentation, and Sarbanes-Oxley requirements.
• Ability to research complex accounting issues, prepare clear technical memoranda, and
translate conclusions into operational requirements and executive communications.
• Experience leading Forms 10-K and 10-Q and related reporting processes for a large,
complex, or multinational public company.

counsel, and cross-functional communication.

talent, and make difficult decisions when facts or deadlines require it.

solely on formal authority.
• Comfort operating in an environment where the work is visible, deadlines are immovable,
facts may evolve, and the consequences of weak judgment or imprecise communication
can be significant.
• A practical mindset that respects technical requirements while understanding business
objectives, operational realities, and the need for scalable execution.

Required Education and Training

IV is the statistical subject matter expert working in cross-functional teams, managing
roadmaps and priorities to ensure timely and high quality delivery of results. This role serves as
a nearly independent statistical lead, providing technical leadership by improving analysis
processes, mentoring junior staff, and managing a diverse project portfolio to ensure that
clinical evidence meets the highest standards for regulatory submissions and scientific

sections with supervision for regulatory submissions, compliance, scientific journals, and

applications.

The Supplier Engineer (Single Port) is responsible for ensuring suppliers reliably support production manufacturing lines by meeting Intuitive Surgical’s requirements for quality, delivery, capacity, cost, and service. Provide data-driven supplier health updates and recommendations with minimal supervision
Perform other related duties as assigned
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or equivalent experience (advanced degree preferred)

Experience supporting high-volume manufacturing environments, preferably in medical devices or regulated industries

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Project
Experience with ERP systems such as SAP or Agile preferred
Experience with Minitab or statistical analysis software is a plus

Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (approximately 25%)

location: USA-Colorado-Louisville; CAN-Alberta-Edmonton
description:
Job Description:
Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for an Breakthrough Innovation Manager to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry. Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company.
Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
Champion Petfoods is looking for a curious, creative and highly collaborative marketer to help shape the future of pet nutrition.
The Global Marketing Breakthrough Innovation Manager will identify emerging needs and new-to-category opportunities by connecting consumer insights, scientific discovery, market signals and ideas from across the Mars ecosystem.
This role focuses on the earliest stages of innovation: finding promising spaces, developing concepts and validating them with consumers and cross-functional partners.
Once an opportunity is sufficiently defined and validated, the role will prepare a clear handoff to the Global Innovation Managers, who will lead development and commercialization.
The Breakthrough Innovation Manager works out of our Corporate office in either Edmonton, AB or Louisville, CO on a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person.
What a typical day looks like
Scan for emerging consumer needs, technologies, ingredients, behaviors and category shifts across pet care, human food and adjacent sectors.
Build relationships across the Mars ecosystem to exchange ideas, find relevant expertise and uncover potential innovation opportunities.
Partner closely with the R&I Discovery team to explore scientific advances, capabilities and early-stage solutions that could address future pet and pet parent needs.
Work with Consumer and Market Insights (CMI) to turn consumer, market and cultural insights into opportunity areas and distinctive concepts.
Create and refine breakthrough concepts, including the consumer problem, target audience, core proposition, potential benefit and reasons to believe.
Design and coordinate learning plans to test assumptions and validate concepts with consumers and internal partners.
Connect insights from different sources to identify patterns, challenge conventional thinking and reveal opportunities that may not be obvious within the pet food category alone.
Assess the strategic fit, potential relevance and early feasibility of opportunities with partners across Brand, R&I, Supply, Regulatory and other functions.
Maintain a forward-looking pipeline of opportunity areas, concepts, evidence and key learning.
Prepare concise recommendations for leadership and innovation governance forums.
Develop clear handoff briefs for Innovation Managers, including the opportunity, consumer evidence, concept direction, assumptions, risks and recommended next steps.
Stay connected with receiving Innovation Managers during handoff to support continuity of the concept and its supporting rationale.
What you'll bring
5+ years of experience in marketing, innovation, consumer insights, strategy, foresight or a related field. Ideally in breakthrough natural or human food industry.
Experience developing consumer-led ideas, concepts or new growth opportunities.
Strong creative thinking and the ability to explore possibilities beyond familiar category conventions.
A talent for connecting information across consumers, markets, science, technology and business needs.
Strong collaboration and networking skills, including the confidence to build relationships across teams and functions.
Comfort working with ambiguity and turning early, incomplete signals into clear questions and testable concepts.
Experience partnering with insights, R&I or other technical teams is an advantage.
Experience in consumer packaged goods, premium/natural food, pet care or another innovation-led industry is an advantage.
Clear communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to explain an opportunity and the evidence behind it.
Curiosity, adaptability and a willingness to learn through experimentation.
How success will be measured
