Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

This team is central to delivering Fabric as a complete, end-to-end intelligence platform.​

OneLake is the open data lake at the heart of Microsoft Fabric and the data foundation for the AI agents built on it. Enterprise data rarely lives in one place. How do you keep metadata in sync with many external catalogs, bridge open table formats like Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, and enforce one consistent security model across all of it? As a Engineer, you'll drive the architecture for these answers, own critical services end to end, work directly with our largest enterprise customers, and mentor engineers around you.

The Global Customer Success (GCS) organization is leading the effort to create the desired customer experience through support offer creation, driving digital transformation across our tools, and delivering operational excellence across CE&S.
As a Cloud Solution Architect aligned to the Azure Analytics platform for Microsoft's Customer Experience & Success (CE&S) organization, you will enable customers to achieve their outcomes based on their investments in Microsoft technology. Leveraging your Microsoft Azure Fabric, Azure Databricks and Power BI technical subject matter expertise, you will lead technical conversations with customers and Microsoft colleagues, driving value to their organization. This is a hands-on role that includes accelerating customer adoption by building Analytics solutions and identifying resolutions to unblock customer success projects for the Analytics Factory. You will also drive product influence with Engineering through technical feedback via the Factory and increase technical intensity with the Field account teams. This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth, honing your technical and program management skills, and deepen your cloud expertise.
The Microsoft Customer Experience & Success (CE&S) organization is responsible for the strategy, design, and implementation of Microsoft’s end-to-end customer experience. Come join CE&S and help us build a future where customers come to us not only because we provide industry-leading products and services, but also because we provide differentiated and connected customer experience.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Deliver secure, resilient, and AI-enabled solutions that help customers achieve business goals, adopt new capabilities, and increase usage and consumption.
Identify opportunities to expand cloud consumption and Unified support by connecting customer needs and industry trends to measurable business value.
Resolve deployment blockers and manage technical risks across customer, partner, and Microsoft teams to accelerate value realization and improve satisfaction.
Share customer feedback and delivery insights to improve products, develop repeatable partner solutions, and strengthen team capabilities.
Customer-Centric Approach:
Play a pivotal role in the Analytics Factory, providing technical enablement, operational support, and strategic engagement across customer projects. This role is designed to ensure successful delivery of Azure Analytics and Data solutions, troubleshoot complex issues, and support innovation through pilot evaluations and advanced use case development. Understand customers' overall data estate, business priorities, and IT success measures.
Facilitate scalable delivery through strong technical program management utilizing a factory model/approach, driving program awareness and demand across the regional operating units.  Attend in-flight project status meetings to monitor progress and identify support needs. Engage directly with complex or non-standard customer use cases beyond existing accelerators. Participate in intake reviews for milestone sizing, objection handling, and technical scoping.

Business Impact:

Operational Awareness: Understanding of consumption metrics and their reflection on program effectiveness. Ability to collaborate with local teams for nominations and intake support.
Unblock Customer Challenges: Leverage subject matter expertise to identify resolutions for customer blockers. Follow best practices and utilize repeatable IP.
Identify and contribute repeatable IP and assets that create velocity in deployment and drives customer value from their Unified investment. Continuously look to improve upon these assets utilizing the best of field inputs. Evaluate pilot opportunities for potential integration into existing offerings.
Architect Analytics Solutions: Apply technical knowledge to design solutions aligned with business and IT needs. Create Innovate with AI roadmaps, lead POCs and MVPs, and ensure long-term technical viability.

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Liberal Arts, or related field AND 4+ years experience in cloud/infrastructure technologies, information technology (IT) consulting/support, systems administration, network operations, software development/support, technology solutions, practice development, architecture, and/or consulting OR equivalent experience.

OR equivalent experience.

Hands-on experience with data warehousing, big data, analytics workloads (Azure or equivalent) and semantic model development with knowledge of key differentiation to determine best fit for use cases and applications
Knowledge of Business Intelligence and design and build of Advanced Analytics and Big Data solutions
Knowledge and understanding of all pillars of Data & AI – Data (RDBMS, NoSQL), Analytics, and AI/ML
Experience with design and creation of technical assets, such as solution accelerators, GitHub repositories

description:
About the Team

The Supply Chain Technology team within OpenAI's Enterprise Platform & Technology organization builds the systems and data foundations that support our supply chain and partner operations. We connect enterprise applications, improve operational visibility, and automate workflows across planning, purchasing, manufacturing, inventory, fulfillment, and returns. We work closely with engineering and business teams to build reliable systems that can evolve with OpenAI's growth.

About the Role

We are seeking an Integrations Architect to set technical direction for enterprise integrations, with a strong focus on supply chain and external partner ecosystems. You will help evolve a growing integration portfolio into a scalable, maintainable foundation through clear architecture, reusable patterns, and strong engineering practices. You will also help establish shared integration architecture and reusable foundations needed to support Finance and Supply Chain systems.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will translate business processes into integration designs, evaluate existing implementations, challenge assumptions, and guide improvements from design through production. Your influence will extend across application engineers, integration engineers, platform teams, and business stakeholders.

You will own integration architecture and partner with the engineering team responsible for the shared integration platform. Through clear requirements, working implementations, and operational evidence, you will help shape capabilities that improve how integrations are developed, tested, deployed, observed, and recovered.

In this role, you will:

 - Own integration architecture across enterprise applications, custom services, and external partners, including e-commerce platforms, logistics providers, contract manufacturers, retailers, and distributors.

 - Translate supply chain processes into clear system boundaries, transaction flows, data ownership, interface contracts, and operational requirements.

 - Partner with Finance and engineering teams to establish reusable integration patterns connecting operational and financial systems, with clear data ownership, reconciliation, and auditability.

 - Assess existing integrations and lead a practical modernization roadmap that improves scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost while sustaining business delivery.

 - Establish reference architectures, reusable connectors, API and event standards, data mappings, versioning practices, and documented design decisions. Lead design and code reviews and mentor engineers.

 - Select appropriate API, messaging, EDI, orchestration, and batch patterns, balancing platform capabilities with custom development and the needs of each business process.

 - Stay close to implementation by building Python services and reference solutions, reviewing code, resolving difficult production issues, and validating designs through tests and measurable behavior.

 - Define reliability and recovery patterns, including idempotency, retries, reconciliation, replay, and continuity planning. Establish operational objectives and ownership across system boundaries.

 - Enable observability that follows business transactions across systems, connecting technical execution to business outcomes and supporting diagnosis, safe recovery, and ongoing improvement.

 - Turn integration delivery experience into prioritized platform requirements and influence shared engineering roadmaps through prototypes, acceptance criteria, and evidence of value.

 - Enable effective AI-assisted development and agentic workflows through well-defined interfaces, testable behavior, explicit approvals, and controls over execution and cost. Apply MCP tools, plugins, or comparable approaches where useful.

 - Embed security, access controls, segregation of duties, auditability, and change management into integration design. Coordinate partner testing, cutover, and operational readiness.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 10+ years of experience in enterprise integration engineering and architecture, including technical leadership for business-critical systems.

 - Understand supply chain processes well enough to independently translate purchasing, receiving, order management, fulfillment, and inventory needs into integrations and explain the operational impact of missing or incorrect transactions.

 - Can support integrations across Supply Chain & Finance systems, working with subject matter experts to translate business processes, reconciliation needs, and financial controls into reliable designs.

 - Have personally shaped architectures, improved existing implementations, and guided engineers toward reusable, maintainable solutions with measurable results.

 - Have deep experience across multiple integration platforms and approaches, including iPaaS and custom services, and can translate their strengths and limitations into useful platform requirements.

 - Are a strong Python engineer who can connect design recommendations to production code, automated tests, deployment practices, and troubleshooting.

 - Understand API and event design, asynchronous messaging, EDI, data contracts, authentication, transaction integrity, and failure recovery across distributed systems.

 - Have built and operated high-volume integrations and can reason about performance, capacity, reliability, observability, and operating cost.

 - Are comfortable with cloud infrastructure, containerized services, version control, CI/CD, and automated integration testing.

 - Can influence technical direction across teams, explain tradeoffs to business stakeholders, and mentor engineers without relying on reporting authority.

 - Work independently, navigate ambiguity, and take responsibility for outcomes from initial design through sustained operation.

 - Integrations with Oracle Fusion ERP or SCM and adjacent enterprise applications such as warehouse, transportation, planning, or product lifecycle management systems.

OpenAI’s Transformation Leads help customers rethink what their business could do with AI. We work with executives and Heads of AI to build business reinvention roadmaps. For this, we provide Leadership Advisory and Collaborative Design support, with the objective to secure and accelerate new business models, including process redesign and culture change.

About the role

You’ll manage our Transformation Leads in America East and personally advise senior customers in New York City. You’ll help a leadership team work through a business or cultural question and leave with a decision they can act on. When the question calls for deeper work, you’ll design and own the workshop that follows. You’ll be based in New York City and meet customers across the US East region.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead executive workshops where leaders try AI on their own work, as they might with an AI chief of staff. In change workshops, bring the people who do the work together to redesign a process, question an incentive, or test a new offering. Agree on who will try it and how they’ll judge the result.

 - Represent OpenAI on stages in front of large audiences and in smaller leadership meetings. Develop original ideas from customer work and bring them to life in talks and internal and external media contributions such as blog articles and podcasts.

 - Bring Product a concrete example of how a customer’s needs are changing. Work with the account team on the customer plan, while our Applied AI Architects and Forward-Deployed Engineers lead the technical work and our Deployment Leads ensure the rollout.

 - Build and manage the East team while carrying your own customer engagements. Assign priorities, support them with your presence and guidance and coach them to excel in their role.

 - Work with regional peers and partners to share approaches that led to customers’ success. Help the customer develop the human system of governance that can lead this change and any other in the future.

You might thrive in this role if:

 - You have helped executives rethink a product, service, or way of working with AI. You can explain what people had to change and what the customer learned by trying it, and you can tie it to concrete value realization.

 - You can inspire a large audience and earn the trust of a fortune 100 executive team. You ask insightful questions and adapt to fluid situations both internally and externally with customers within a tight delivery schedule.

 - You use AI yourself and can turn an ambitious idea into a small, credible test with a customer in a matter of minutes in every industry, LoB or function.

 - Have managed customer-facing teams while leading customer work yourself. You can name a decision someone you coached made on their own and was successful beyond both your expectations and theirs.

The Hardware Marketing team helps people understand what OpenAI’s hardware products can do and how they can fit into everyday life. We work with Product Marketing, Design, Creative, Sales, and Operations to bring products to market and create experiences where people can try them for themselves.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Visual Merchant to shape how customers discover, understand, and try OpenAI hardware in stores. Reporting to the Channel Lead, you’ll own visual merchandising for OpenAI-owned experiences and third-party retail. You’ll work with Creative, Design, and retail partners to build displays that tell a clear product story and make it easy for customers to get hands-on.

You’ll take the work from concept through installation, setting a standard in our own spaces and adapting it for partner stores. You’ll be as comfortable giving feedback on a prototype as you are walking a store to see what customers notice, touch, and miss.

In this role, you will:

 - Make the product story visible. Set the order in which customers see products, signage, and demos. Work with Product Marketing and Creative to keep claims accurate and give customers a clear place to start.

 - Turn standards into tools store teams can use. Create layout guides, fixture and signage specifications, and setup and reset instructions. Partner with Production and Retail Operations on prototypes, installation, and quality checks so displays are safe and can be maintained day to day.

 - Use what you see in stores to improve the work. Watch how customers approach and use displays, gather feedback from store teams, and check whether installations match the brief. Use what you learn to fix issues and update the next rollout.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Built visual merchandising for physical retail and can show how you took work from concept through installation. Experience with both brand-owned and partner stores is a plus.

 - Made a complex product easy to discover and try through strong spatial layout, signage, and demo presentation. Experience with consumer technology or hands-on product demos is a plus.

7+ years in analytics, analytics engineering, or data engineering, with stakeholder-facing delivery.

Strong SQL skills and experience with dbt or an equivalent transformation framework, ELT patterns, and lakehouse data models.
Experience building BI or executive dashboards and explaining data clearly to senior stakeholders.

location: Tustin, California
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary The Project Manager, Asset Management, leads cross-functional asset-management projects and operating workstreams for Specialized Programs in Engineering Quality. The role establishes structure around vehicle demand, asset data, fleet readiness, logistics, lifecycle decisions, and program execution across Engineering, Commercial Fleet, Communications, Marketing, Events, Service, Compliance, and partner functions. This role converts complex or ambiguous program needs into executable plans, operating mechanisms, and measurable outcomes. It is accountable for improving the reliability of the asset-management system—not only completing individual vehicle transactions. The Project Manager, Asset Manager is expected to operate with substantial autonomy in the domain, provide recommendations to leaders, identify systemic risks, and influence stakeholders without formal people-management authority. It remains a professional individual-contributor role. Responsibilities Core accountability Own and improve assigned asset-management programs from intake through lifecycle closure, ensuring that: Fleet demand is translated into clear priorities, allocation recommendations, and executable plans. Vehicle and VIN data is accurate, governed, and usable for operational and leadership decisions. Asset movements, assignments, locations, readiness, ownership, and lifecycle status are visible across systems. Cross-functional projects have aligned scope, milestones, dependencies, decision rights, risks, and closure criteria. Engineering, Communications, Marketing, Events, Logistics, Service, Compliance, Facilities, and Real Estate are aligned to program timing and requirements. Audit and fleet-cleanup findings are converted into prioritized action plans with measurable closure. Operating processes are standardized, documented, and improved based on recurring issues and lessons learned. Primary responsibilities Asset portfolio strategy and fleet-data governance Establish and maintain a reliable asset-management view across Engineering test vehicles, benchmark vehicles, prototypes, Special Projects, Adventure Fleet, Communications media loans, Marketing, and Commercial Fleet. Define the required data fields, documentation standards, ownership rules, photo requirements, and reconciliation cadence for VIN-level records. Lead multi-site fleet audits and asset-reconciliation programs across locations such as Torrance, 9750, and Myford 2. Analyze asset data to identify aging records, assignment conflicts, unplanned locations, stale statuses, readiness gaps, underused vehicles, and lifecycle risks. Recommend disposition, reassignment, transfer, decommission, remarketing, donation/loaner, or museum-transfer actions based on documented facts and functional input. Maintain governance for Garage/Fleet Management, Jira, dashboards, inventory records, and related project trackers. Define and monitor data-quality controls so that VIN, location, ownership, assignee, use case, status, and lifecycle stage remain consistent across systems. Create executive-ready summaries of asset exposure, operational risk, demand, and corrective-action progress. Program and project leadership Lead projects from intake, discovery, and scope definition through planning, execution, handoff, reconciliation, and closure. Translate ambiguous or competing requirements into a prioritized workstream plan with milestones, owners, decision points, risks, dependencies, and resource needs. Establish project operating cadence, including status reviews, action tracking, decision logs, issue escalation, and closure reviews. Coordinate across Engineering, technicians, fabricators, shop managers, project leads, Procurement, Logistics, Facilities, Real Estate, Service, Compliance, Events, Communications, Marketing, and Commercial Fleet. Lead workback planning for content shoots, press drives, media loans, brand activations, launch events, benchmark activities, and other multi-vehicle programs. Identify schedule, cost, readiness, capacity, and asset-availability tradeoffs and provide recommendations before they become execution failures. Drive closure of cross-functional blockers when no single stakeholder owns the full end-to-end outcome. Capture lessons learned and convert recurring problems into process, system, or governance improvements. Vehicle demand, allocation, and readiness governance Manage the intake and prioritization process for specialized-program vehicle requests, including engineering, media, marketing, event, launch, benchmark, prototype, and partner needs. Develop allocation recommendations based on vehicle availability, program criticality, readiness, timing, cost, risk, and lifecycle considerations. Participate in vehicle-ranking discussions and communicate decisions, constraints, and unresolved tradeoffs to affected stakeholders. Establish readiness criteria for license plates, registration, insurance, cleanliness, charging, repairs, service, modifications, training, prototype-driver certification, and approvals. Coordinate readiness reviews and exception management for multi-vehicle deployments. Communicate when requested fixes or asset changes cannot fit the timing of a media loan, content shoot, event, or other committed milestone. Ensure that post-use activities—including return, inspection, reassignment, repair, data update, and lifecycle disposition—are included in the original plan. Logistics, movement, and lifecycle execution Lead the integrated plan for vehicle allocation, shipping, receiving, transportation, handoffs, event delivery, onsite support, return logistics, and final reconciliation. Coordinate shipping and receiving providers and establish clear custody, documentation, timing, and exception-resolution expectations. Lead complex or multi-site vehicle movements involving Engineering, Special Projects, Communications media loans, Commercial Fleet, Adventure Fleet, and other asset groups. Support decommissioning, reassignment, remarketing, disposal, donations/loaners, museum transfers, and other lifecycle activities through documented decision paths. Ensure movements and lifecycle decisions are reflected in the system of record and supported by appropriate evidence. Identify systemic logistics issues and recommend changes to vendors, processes, service-level expectations, or operating cadence. Engineering and Commercial Fleet interface Act as a senior asset-management point of contact between Engineering, Vehicle Development, Fleet Operations, Logistics, Service, Compliance, Communications, Marketing, Events, and Commercial Fleet. Establish clear transition criteria for vehicles moving through Special Projects use cases before entering the Commercial Asset group. Coordinate ad hoc vehicle needs involving modifications, movie/media preparation, testing, content, and other specialized use cases. Ensure vehicles are routed through Jira and the appropriate fleet workflow before Commercial Asset assignment or other downstream use. Lead transition planning for vehicles entering Communications media loans and vehicles moving into Commercial Fleet after an event. Resolve ownership, priority, timing, and readiness conflicts using documented facts and escalation pathways. Provide leadership with recommendations when demand exceeds available vehicles, capacity, timing, or readiness. Jira, workflow, and operating governance Own the operating model for the applicable Jira board supporting specialized-program vehicle and asset work. Define intake requirements, workflow states, ownership, service expectations, acceptance criteria, and closure evidence. Ensure vehicle requests involving modifications, movie/media preparation, testing, or Commercial Asset assignment are traceable from request through closure. Review Jira and auto-ticket information against actual vehicle status, planned location, owner, assignee, readiness, and use case. Use the Engineering Fleet Hub as a source of truth for requests, compliance, guidelines, training, dashboards, and reporting. Establish repeatable governance for safety, audits, transportation, readiness, stakeholder responsiveness, and lifecycle controls. Identify opportunities to automate reporting, reduce duplicate entry, improve dashboards, or strengthen data controls. Audit, risk, and compliance leadership Define audit scope, sampling, evidence requirements, responsibilities, due dates, and closure standards. Lead physical audits using VIN lists, photographs, vehicle descriptions, location data, and space-status documentation. Maintain a risk-based view of missing assets, conflicting assignments, unapproved use, lost custody, readiness gaps, and compliance exposure. Escalate safety, regulatory, insurance, registration, security, or material business risks with facts, impacts, options, and recommendations. Verify that audit findings are not only corrected in the system but also resolved operationally and supported by evidence. Expectations applied to this role Ownership and autonomy Independently lead complex, cross-functional asset-management projects and recurring operating mechanisms. Own outcomes across functional boundaries, even when individual tasks are performed by other teams. Determine the appropriate planning approach, cadence, tools, and stakeholders for each assignment. Operate effectively with incomplete information, making reasonable assumptions visible and validating them with the right owners. Provide manager-level visibility into progress, risk, capacity, tradeoffs, and decisions without requiring step-by-step direction. Problem solving and judgment Diagnose systemic causes—not only individual execution issues—across fleet data, logistics, readiness, lifecycle, and stakeholder workflows. Develop practical options and recommendations when priorities, timing, vehicles, or resources conflict. Make sound decisions within delegated authority and escalate decisions involving material safety, compliance, cost, schedule, or policy risk. Anticipate downstream effects of assignment, location, readiness, and lifecycle decisions. Use data, audit evidence, stakeholder input, and operational context to distinguish urgent exceptions from process problems requiring structural correction. Influence and communication Influence stakeholders across Engineering, Fleet Operations, Logistics, Service, Compliance, Communications, Marketing, Events, Facilities, and Real Estate without relying on direct authority. Facilitate alignment when priorities conflict and document the rationale for decisions. Communicate clearly at both the working-team and leadership level, adapting detail to the audience. Present risks and recommendations with business impact, timing, alternatives, and a clear decision request. Establish trust by maintaining accurate information, honoring commitments, and escalating early. Planning and delivery Lead planning for projects with multiple workstreams, locations, vehicle types, dependencies, and stakeholder groups. Integrate asset availability, readiness, logistics, budget or cost implications, safety, compliance, and lifecycle requirements into a single delivery plan. Hold workstream owners accountable to milestones and closure criteria through clear operating cadence. Replan effectively when scope, vehicle availability, timing, or program requirements change. Deliver sustainable outcomes that remain accurate after the immediate project or event is complete. Process improvement and organizational contribution Identify recurring failure modes and implement improvements to workflows, templates, dashboards, controls, and documentation. Create scalable standards for VIN documentation, asset reconciliation, Jira intake, readiness reviews, vehicle transitions, and project closure. Share lessons learned and enable coordinators and partner teams to follow improved processes. Contribute to team-level planning and operating-model development. Serve as a domain resource for asset-management fundamentals and specialized- program fleet execution. Expected recurring deliverables Governed VIN-level fleet and asset portfolio view. Multi-site audit plan, findings dashboard, risk assessment, and reconciliation closure log. Demand-intake and vehicle-allocation recommendations. Integrated workback plans for media, marketing, engineering, event, content, and partner programs. Jira operating model, intake standards, workflow definitions, and closure reporting. Vehicle readiness review, exception log, and decision record. Cross-functional status reports showing milestones, risks, dependencies, tradeoffs, and decisions needed. Asset transition and lifecycle plan for reassignment, decommissioning, remarketing, donation/loaner, museum transfer, or Commercial Fleet entry. Data-quality and process-improvement roadmap. End-of-project reconciliation, lessons learned, and operating handoff. Measures of success Leadership and program teams can make decisions using accurate, timely, and traceable fleet data. Asset records remain accurate across systems after vehicles move, change owners, change use, or complete a program. Vehicle demand is prioritized transparently against availability, criticality, readiness, timing, cost, and risk. Complex deployments and transitions are executed with fewer avoidable escalations, missed handoffs, and last-minute readiness gaps. Audit findings are prioritized by risk and closed with verified operational and system evidence. Jira and Engineering Fleet Hub workflows provide clear ownership, status, accountability, and reporting. Cross-functional stakeholders understand decisions, constraints, tradeoffs, and next actions. Recurring fleet and asset issues are reduced through process, data, vendor, or governance improvements. Vehicles move cleanly between Special Projects, Engineering, Adventure Fleet, Communications, Marketing, and Commercial Fleet. Safety, compliance, training, and lifecycle requirements remain protected when schedule pressure increases. The role produces durable systems and standards, not only one-time project completion. Role boundaries and escalation triggers This role may lead planning, coordinate execution, establish operating mechanisms, analyze data, and recommend decisions. It should escalate when work involves: Safety, regulatory, insurance, registration, security, or compliance exposure. Material cost, capacity, schedule, event-readiness, or business-continuity risk. Unclear asset ownership, conflicting business-use claims, or disputed prioritization. Vehicle damage, missing assets, unapproved use, or loss of custody. Disposition decisions requiring functional, legal, finance, compliance, or executive approval. Policy exceptions or decisions outside delegated authority. Cross-functional conflict that cannot be resolved through documented facts, agreed priorities, or established governance. Escalations should include the current condition, business impact, options considered, recommendation, decision owner, and required timing. Qualifications Strong working knowledge of asset management, fleet operations, vehicle lifecycle processes, logistics, project/program management, and operational governance. Ability to manage and interpret VIN-level data, audit evidence, dashboards, and cross- system records. Demonstrated ability to lead complex workback plans, risk registers, action logs,b decision records, and executive-ready status reporting. Comfort using Jira, fleet-management systems, dashboards, spreadsheets, and shared documentation tools as operating systems rather than passive trackers. Strong influence, facilitation, negotiation, and cross-functional communication skills. Ability to identify systemic problems and implement practical process or data improvements. Sound judgment under schedule pressure and willingness to escalate material risks early. Ability to coach or enable coordinators and partner teams through clear standards and repeatable processes, without requiring formal people-management responsibility. title: Accounts Payable/Receivable Associate
location: US (Remote)
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll be the person who keeps money moving in and out of Standard Bots accurately and on time — paying vendors, invoicing customers, and making sure the books can stand up to an audit. We build industrial robots that make automation flexible for modern manufacturers, and as we scale, the finance engine behind that growth needs someone sharp, careful, and good with people. That's you.

📍 Location - this position is remote and open to candidates anywhere in the United States. Unfortunately, we're not able to support visas for this role. 


What you'll do

- Own accounts payable day to day: process vendor invoices accurately and on time, with the right coding and approvals every time.

- Set up and maintain vendors, including collecting W-9s, so records are clean from the start.

- Prepare and run payments through Ramp.

- Support month-end close on the AP side.

- Own accounts receivable invoicing: create and send customer invoices that match contract terms.

- Work with internal teams and customers to resolve billing questions quickly and clearly.

- Support collections while keeping customer relationships professional and positive.

- Keep accurate records and supporting documentation so we're ready for audit and compliance needs.

- Pitch in on sales tax, expense reporting, and other ad hoc accounting projects as they come up.

- Work closely with Operations, Sales, and Finance, because good finance work depends on all three.


What you'll bring

- 2–4 years of experience in accounts payable and/or accounts receivable.

- A strong eye for detail and the organizational habits to back it up.

- Working knowledge of basic accounting principles and internal controls.

- The ability to juggle multiple priorities without dropping the ball.

- Clear written and verbal communication, whether you're chasing down an approval or explaining an invoice to a customer.

- Experience with accounting systems, ideally QuickBooks Online.


Nice to have

- Familiarity with tools like Ramp, Stripe, or similar platforms.


Why you'll like it here

- You'll be part of a rapidly growing robotics company, building something physical and real.

- You'll take on a high-impact role supporting core finance operations, not a corner of the work nobody looks at.

- You'll work with a collaborative, low-ego team.

- You'll have room to grow alongside the company as finance operations scale.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $50,000 to $67,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Staff Hardware Test & Validation Lead (On-site)
location: Glen Cove, NY
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots, shipping at scale to customers ranging from small manufacturers to some of the largest companies in the country. We're hiring a technical lead to build and run a central hardware testing function to support product development across the company. You'll set and maintain a high bar for product quality, plan and resource test work, build and run setups from quick bench rigs to long-running validation at scale, and help the team troubleshoot and root-cause failures. The work covers robotic and electromechanical systems of all kinds. Hands-on IC technical lead role, working closely with the mechanical, electrical, and software engineering teams.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Test Process and Quality Standards. Guide and build a test and validation team, working closely with the hardware team. Standardize how hardware product validation is planned and run, and work with the hardware team to set quality standards. Help turn requirements and specs into test plans.

Planning and Scheduling. Plan and schedule test work and assign lab space, equipment, and people to it. Work closely with hardware and software teams on priorities and timing.

Testbeds, Fixtures, and Ad-Hoc Testing. Help review, design and build complex testbeds and fixtures, including mechanical design, instrumentation, and data acquisition. Run one-off tests from a spec or setup the hardware team provides, and scale them up when needed.

Product Validation and Long-Running Tests. Stand up and run product validation testing across many units, from component qualification to system-level performance tests. Define stop conditions, data products, and post-run inspection, and keep long tests running.

Documentation and Analysis. Strong documentation is a core skill for this role. Write test reports and analysis, procedures, and initial failure analysis. Keep documentation accurate and up to date.

Troubleshooting and Root Cause. Help mechanical and electrical engineers analyze complex failures and perform maintenance to keep hardware running. Engage with engineering teams to respond to and resolve failures.


TOOLS

Sensors and sensing (encoders, IMUs, accelerometers, image processing), data loggers & data collection interfaces, SolidWorks & PDM, oscilloscopes, thermal instrumentation, programming for data processing and analysis, Claude Code (or similar AI tools), typical business and productivity tools (Notion, Asana, Google Docs).


WHAT WE NEED


REQUIRED

 - BS in ME, EE, or similar (or equivalent experience)

 - 5+ years in hardware testing or validation, ideally in robotics, automotive, aerospace, medical, or a similar regulated or safety-critical domain

 - Experience taking complex validation plans from system requirements through test design, execution, and reporting

 - Experience leading and organizing test work, including planning, prioritizing, and assigning lab resources and people

 - Experience with root-cause investigations across ME / EE / FW boundaries

 - Comfortable writing test plans with clear pass/fail criteria and choosing sample sizes based on confidence needs

 - Hands-on with electrical instrumentation (scopes, probes, etc.) and reading schematics

 - Mechanical fundamentals including tolerance stacks, motor analysis, power transmission, bearings, fits, and structural design

 - Strong written documentation habits and experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Collaborative or industrial robots, or 6-DOF motion systems

 - Functional safety standards: ISO 13849, ISO 10218, IEC 61508, or ISO 26262

 - Mechanical / electrical design of fixtures and tooling

 - DFMEA / PFMEA or formal reliability practices

 - Failure analysis and root-cause analysis


WHERE THE ROLE GROWS

Over time, the role can expand to include:

 - Cross-Platform Test Strategy: own test strategy across platforms and set common test methods for every program

 - Lab Capability and Infrastructure: expand testing range and scope, plus test automation, fleet monitoring, and supporting infrastructure

 - Reliability Program: track MTBF / B-life and feed corrective actions back to design

 - Phase Gates and Design Reviews: represent testing at EVT/DVT/PVT gates and in DFMEA/PFMEA reviews

 - Technical Mentorship: mentor test engineers and technicians as the group grows

Compensation and Benefits:

The base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $200,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

description:

Ability to learn quickly

Strong interpersonal skills
Ability to work as part of a team
Ability to build relationships
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits.  Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation that accrues starting at .01961 hours based on a 40 hour week up to 40 hours annually ( 64 hours in California) after an introductory period, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 or 30 hours worked, depending on work location), and additional pay if working on one of eight observed holidays. title: Account Executive Product, Crypto/Stablecoins
location: SF, NYC
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Bridge team helps businesses build and scale stablecoin-powered financial products and global money movement through a single API. Our virtual accounts let international consumers and businesses access, store, and spend US dollars, while our payouts infrastructure helps platforms disburse funds globally.
We collaborate across product, compliance, legal, and operations as we develop Stripe Crypto’s go-to-market approach and build a durable sales culture. Our team has built financial infrastructure at Coinbase, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, and Airbnb, and we’re focused on making stablecoins a practical foundation for global payments.
What you’ll do
As an Account Executive (New Business), you’ll help grow Bridge by turning qualified demand and outbound prospecting into successful customer relationships. You’ll own the commercial journey from first conversation through launch, translating business and technical needs into practical solutions and working with internal partners to deliver strong outcomes. You’ll also use data and field insights to improve how the team sells and how Stripe Crypto scales.
Responsibilities
Close qualified inbound leads and develop outbound opportunities through networking, cold calling, and lead follow-up
Lead discovery conversations to understand prospects’ business needs and identify relevant Bridge solutions
Manage the full sales cycle, from identifying opportunities through negotiation and close, and partner with customers and internal teams to get them live
Build and maintain client relationships that support satisfaction, repeat business, and account growth
Meet or exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual sales targets while providing detailed and accurate sales forecasts
Collaborate with product, risk, operations, and other internal teams to deliver effective solutions for clients
Lead and contribute to team projects that develop and refine the sales process and help shape the Bridge and Stripe sales culture
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
3-8 years of sales experience managing the full sales cycle for new accounts at a high-growth payments, financial technology, crypto, or technology company
A track record of exceeding sales quotas, closing net-new and upsell opportunities, and managing complex pricing or commercial negotiations

The Batch Compute Experience team owns the platform that Stripe engineers use to build, run, debug and optimize Apache Spark jobs. Hundreds of engineers and thousands of production jobs driving critical business processes, such as payouts and reconciliations, run on this platform.
Today, diagnosing and tuning a job means reasoning by hand across scattered telemetry, configuration, query plans and application code. Our goal is to make Spark at Stripe fast to iterate, reliable by default, and self-optimizing, so engineers can focus on business logic instead of Spark internals. We're doing this through three connected efforts:
Modernization : keeping Stripe's Spark runtime and dependency stack current, including Spark 3.5 → Spark 4, Scala 2.13 and Apache Iceberg. We're building automated upgrade and validation tools so that upgrading the whole fleet becomes routine and low-risk instead of a multi-year manual effort
Agentic Spark and optimization : building trustworthy, AI-powered workflows that diagnose failed or underperforming jobs, recommend fixes based on evidence, and carry them safely into configuration changes, code PRs or escalations. We also want to optimize configuration, query plans and code across the whole fleet
Operational excellence : making the platform reliable, observable and compliant, and defining user-experience metrics that show whether we're succeeding
Over the longer term, we want to turn the platform into a Spark control plane that keeps learning. It should detect problems before users notice them, validate fixes safely and apply them through policy-controlled automation.
What you’ll do
As a Staff Engineer on Batch Compute Experience, you'll set the technical direction for one of Stripe's most widely used data platforms. You'll lead multi-quarter efforts across teams, make high-stakes architectural decisions affecting thousands of production workloads, and raise the engineering bar for the team and its partners.
Responsibilities
Lead Spark modernization across the fleet. Own the technical strategy for moving thousands of production jobs to newer Spark and Iceberg runtimes. This includes target selection, qualification, deciding the rollout unit (cluster, application or hybrid), and rollback planning, while coordinating dependencies with partner infrastructure teams
Make upgrades continuous and safe. Design and evolve automated upgrade and validation systems: shadow execution against production data, output-correctness comparison, sandboxed execution, and staged promotion. The goal is to make each new runtime upgrade cheaper than the last
Architect agentic Spark workflows. Build LLM-powered systems that diagnose failures, out-of-memory errors (OOMs), data skew and performance regressions. They should produce evidence-backed recommendations that are backtested and gated in CI, and you'll define the safety, provenance and human-approval requirements for every automated action
Build safe configuration and remediation paths. Design authorized, validated, reversible no-code configuration changes, along with pipelines that detect anti-patterns across the fleet and open code-fix PRs or tickets
Drive efficiency at scale. Identify, prove out and roll out the highest-value configuration and query-plan optimizations, such as shuffle and adaptive query execution (AQE) tuning, executor sizing, join strategy and partitioning. Turn the measured gains into real infrastructure savings without hurting correctness or reliability
Improve the developer experience. Shorten the inner dev loop, improve PySpark support and observability (including Python memory diagnostics), and unify how jobs are packaged and launched across schedulers such as Airflow and Flyte
Set the technical bar. Lead critical design reviews, define reliability standards (SLOs, observability, testing) for the services we own, mentor senior engineers, and steer the team away from structural and operational debt

title: Senior/Staff Product Designer
location: SF Bay Area
description:
ABOUT TYBA

Tyba is a modeling platform for energy companies developing, financing, and operating renewable energy infrastructure. Energy companies rely on technical models daily to make crucial infrastructure decisions and operate their assets.

Our mission is to make cutting-edge models accessible to cross-functional teams so that companies can build and operate more renewable energy more profitably. We are backed by leading climate and generalist VCs and work with many of the industry’s most innovative energy companies.




THE ROLE

Tyba is hiring its first product designer. Traders, asset managers, operators, and analysts use Tyba every day to bid, monitor, and report on battery storage and energy portfolios. A lot of that work still lives in spreadsheets and in our users' heads. You'll figure out what the product should be and make it great: how it's organized, how it looks, and how it shows what our optimizer is doing for customers.

It's a rich design problem: dense, time-sensitive data for expert users making high-stakes decisions. The goal is a tool that's powerful without feeling complicated, where every detail is considered.

We're looking for a senior/staff generalist who sets direction, not just executes it. You'll break down ambiguous problems, decide what's worth solving, and carry the work from first sketch to shipped, with the taste to make it look and feel right. You'll report to the CTO, work as a peer to product and engineering, and lay the foundation for design at Tyba.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead design on our biggest problems. Partner with product and engineering to understand how users work, explore a range of directions, and carry the design from first sketch to shipped.

 - Define how Tyba looks and feels. Build the first design system. Set the visual language and core patterns the product is built on, and work with engineering so they're easy to build consistently. Partner with marketing so product and brand feel like one company.

 - Make dense data easy to act on. Design charts, tables, and workflows that let expert users read complex, time-sensitive information at a glance and act on it with confidence.

 - Get close to users. Spend time with the traders, operators, and analysts who use Tyba, build a real model of how they work, and bring that into every decision.

 - Move at startup pace. Prototype with real data, in code where it helps, and use AI to go faster without skipping the thinking.

 - Shape how we build. Bring a design perspective to roadmap and strategy, and define how design works at Tyba.
   
   


SKILLS & EXPERIENCE





REQUIRED

 - 7+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio of shipped work on real products

 - Strong product thinking: You pick the right problem, break it down, weigh options, and can explain the tradeoffs behind what shipped

 - B2B SaaS experience making dense, complex data clear for expert users: Tables, charts, dashboards, and analytical or workflow tools that replace spreadsheets

 - High ownership: You've driven projects from scoping to ship on lean teams, without waiting on a researcher, PM, or spec

 - High visual and interaction craft: Hierarchy, type, layout, states, edge cases, density

 - Clear communicator who makes complex ideas simple and brings engineering and stakeholders along

 - Thoughtful use of AI in your process: You know when it speeds you up and when it skips the thinking


PREFERRED

 - First or early designer at a startup, or 0→1 work inside a larger company

 - Design leadership experience

 - Ships code or code prototypes

 - Experience in energy, trading, finance, or another complex domain

 - Built or evolved a design system; brand and visual identity fluency

No energy background needed. Curiosity about power markets and how our users work is what matters.




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

 - Salary: $185-235K, depending on experience and qualifications.

 - Benefits: Parental leave, medical benefits, and unlimited PTO.

 - Equity Options: Opportunity to own a stake in the company through an employee stock option plan.
   
   


FAQ




WHAT IS THE INTERVIEW PROCESS LIKE?

Our interview process focuses on core competencies. We want to make sure that you are set up for success at a fast-growing and high-impact startup. We will first get to know each other through conversations about Tyba, your background, and what you are looking for in your next role. While the specifics vary, from there, we will focus on evaluating your skills and experience relevant to the role. Once we have determined whether you are a fit for the team, we will help you get to know the company better and speak with other team members to inform your decision. We prioritize transparency, clear communication, and ensuring that we do our best to find a mutual fit.

Execute a clean handoff to the Account Manager once activation requirements are met.
Meet or exceed assigned activity goals, including outbound call volume.
Maintain complete, accurate, and current prospect, pipeline, and activity records in our CRM and sales engagement platforms.
Represent TA credibly to fleet owners and decision makers.
Complete all required compliance and authorization training on time.

Demonstrated comfort and effectiveness with cold calling and sustained outbound telephone selling.
Proven ability to close net-new business against measurable goals.
Persistence and resilience. This role involves rejection and requires someone who keeps dialing.
Ability to drive a deal past signature through to activation without losing momentum.
Strong working proficiency with CRM platforms, sales engagement tools, and Microsoft Office.
Practical fluency with AI and large language model tools, and a willingness to use them to work more effectively.
Strong quantitative aptitude and comfort with volume, margin, and percentage-based analysis.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

College degree preferred.
Five or more years of sales experience preferred.
Business-to-business sales experience preferred, particularly in new business development.
Experience in transportation, trucking, fuel, or a related industry preferred.

Performance is measured as percent to goal against assigned targets for closed and activated deals, along with outbound activity and on-time completion of required training. A deal counts when the customer is contracted, set up, and fueling.

Process Architecture

Simplify and standardize processes before automation or digitization.

Position Overview
The Parts, Inventory & Finance Product Manager is responsible for ensuring the integrity of parts, inventory, and financial transactions across Truck Service, from shop activity through SAP/ERP posting, reconciliation, and financial close.
The role leads the end-to-end requirements and controls that ensure parts movements, inventory transactions, billing, and related financial activities are accurately brought together and reconciled across D365 Field Service and SAP. The position works closely with Service Platforms, Finance & Accounting, Process & Work Standards, Digital Intelligence, and operational teams to ensure transaction accuracy, control efficiency, and financial readiness.
This is a people leadership role with responsibility for leading the product backlog and driving improvements across parts, inventory, and finance-related processes and systems.
Key Responsibilities
Parts & Inventory Management
Own the end-to-end processes and requirements for catalog management, purchasing, receiving, stocking, transfers, consumption, returns, adjustments, and inventory closeout.
Ensure inventory transactions are accurately reflected across D365 Field Service and SAP.
Govern transaction completeness and accuracy throughout the inventory lifecycle.
Define and maintain the controls required to support effective parts and inventory management.
Identify and address inventory integrity issues, including record discrepancies and aged variances.
SAP/ERP Finance, Billing & Reconciliation
Own priorities and requirements related to billing, invoicing, posting, settlement, reconciliation, and remediation.
Define functional requirements and controls within SAP to support accurate financial processing.
Establish controls for missing, duplicated, rejected, or out-of-balance transactions.
Ensure shop activity flows accurately through the relevant ERP and finance processes.
Partner with Finance & Accounting to align system configuration, controls, and reconciliation requirements with official financial policies.
Bring up material financial-control exceptions and risks to the appropriate Finance decision makers.

Ensure upstream applications meet established transaction, inventory, and financial-control requirements.
Establish appropriate controls for transaction completeness, accuracy, reconciliation, and exception management.

Support reliable integration between operational systems and SAP/ERP.
